title_formula_note: Chosen T6, the creative director's lead (49 chars, 9 words). 'Deadlier' is the one dread word and the 'Deeper' gradient is the scope device. No 'dig' or 'hole' (decisions 2026-10-16), no '?', no 'Creepier the Deeper You Go' (Mr. Science noun-swap ban). Not back-to-back: 019 was T4, and the last T6 was 015, five episodes back. No published title gets reused: 'Why the Ocean...' (006) and 'Why Antarctica...' (016) only ever appeared as alts, and the subject noun 'Ground' is new. Alts for A/B: T6 'Earth' variant (shorter, and 'Earth' reads less Minecraft than 'ground'/'dig'), T2 (Doug survives 3 of 12, so it ranks below the gradient on honesty), T3 'Under Your Feet' (puts the viewer in it), T4 'Living' (pays off at Movile, the Devil Worm and the bacterium, weaker at the core). T1 was dropped because 'What Dying at Every Depth ... Would Be Like' would be a noun swap of 016. T3 avoids 'Discoveries at Every Depth', which would be a swap of 006.

Labels are chapter names (drop to the 8 best if 12 do not read at 168x94) and must not use title or alt-title words: Why, Ground, Earth, Gets, Deadlier, Deeper, Doug, Goes, Die, Depth, Disturbing, Places, Layer, Feet, Creepiest, Scientists, Living, Underground.
description:
Doug heads straight down through the deepest places on Earth: a cave sealed off for millions of years, the deepest mine, the Kola Superdeep Borehole, and then past 12 km, where nobody has ever been, all the way to the center of the Earth. Every stop is deadlier than the last.

Where should we send Doug next? Tell us in the comments.
Subscribe so you don't miss Doug's next bad day.
